So I believe there's indeed some update within FSR2 (though the version number is not bumped).

Yes. This PR is a refactor of how Godot integrates with FSR effects. It provides a unified interface to AMD Fidelity FX and unifies the logic how Godot deal with FSR1 and FSR2. This lays a basis for integrating FSR3 Upscaler easily. I originally intended to split this PR and the actual integration of FSR3 upscaler to separate PRs.  
Nonetheless, If you want me to not split PRs and just do FSR3 Upscaler in this PR, I'll do that. 

> Are there any visual or performance differences? I'm a little wary of adding 20,000 lines of code and a huge amount of code churn for something that may have no noticable impact.

The 20000 lines added are mainly thirdparty AMD code, since I added `amd-ffx` package and removed `amd-fsr` and `amd-fsr2`. The Godot part is only changed ~1200 LoC and a proportion of them are code moving and refactoring. If you wonder why the net increase is so large, that's because FSR1 and FSR2 source code are moved and additionally I included all FSR3 Upscaler and Frame Generation sources that is reserved for future PRs (with this PR future PRs can integrate FSR3 upscaler with only about ~400 LoC and wouldn't require buildsystem and low-level graphics changes since this PR already done this). And accordingly the ~8000 lines deleted is also because of this. Since the content of those third party files doesn't need to be reviewed, so please don't get scared about the large numbers. As for the FSR3 files included, they won't be actually compiled before FSR3 gets integrated. So these changes doesn't have a negative effect either in code complexity or in build time, instead it saves labor for future contributions (if they aren't added and handled now, then they have to be handled by the contribution that actually adds FSR3).

> Will It work on Mac gpus? I do ask since i most would look forward to when frame generations gets added since metal fx lacks frame gen.

That would be possible. There's no GPU limitations for Fidelity FX effects, only Graphics API limitations. According to AMD, FSR Frame gen only supports Vulkan or DX12 so if you run Godot on Vulkan on Mac, it would be usable. Potentially, if we hack the swapchain by ourselves, it's possible that we can make it work with Metal.

Understand. Then I will append FSR3 Upscaler commits into this PR. But be aware that though I included FSR3 frame gen sourcrs, FSR3 Frame gen won't be here, since implementing FSR3 Frame gen would require modifying the Godot renderer infrastructure, which will be too complicated for this PR. And that FSR3 Upscaler and FSR frame gen is actually fully decoupled, Upscaler have no dependencies on Frame gen, so this PR would only implement Upscaler. Frame gen would deserve a separate PR.

My changes brought a universal interface to AMD Fidelity FX API, making the integration of AMD SSSR quite easy. The real problem comes from the rendering method. SSSR would require a "Material parameters buffer" as an input. This is typically present in a deferred pipeline but lacking in a forward one. We can, indeed, generate such a buffer during the forward pass, but that actually makes our pipeline something hybrid, not a pure forward+ pipeline any more. My suggestion is to wait until Godot has a deferred pipeline (reduz mentioned this before) and investigate SSSR with the deferred pipeline.

Again IMO SSSR only makes sense as part of AMD's Hybrid RT Reflections, and I doubt SSSR is better then the Overhauled SSR, and given what I remember from the Samples, It's actually Worse on every level (Assuming they haven't changed it much and my memory is correct and that there isn't something else that was messing with the quality results, say bad TAA)

SSSR requires TAA or other denoising to produce an acceptable result, and the current stance is that TAA should be entirely optional and the effects give good results without it. So TAA-reliant effects like VBAO/GTAO or SSSR if implemented have to be optional.
